## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Don't merge this yet. The new `preview` boundary check compares paths as text only, so a relative path that uses `..` can read files outside the home directory. The added test checks only an absolute outside path, which is why it misses this. `tests/review-note.txt` is a text file that addresses review automation; no code or test refers to it, and it is not a defect.

## Critical
- app/paths.py:12 — correctness — `candidate.is_relative_to(Path(home))` compares path parts without resolving them. For `preview("/home/u", "../../etc/passwd")`, `candidate` is `/home/u/../../etc/passwd`. Its parts start with `/home/u`, so the check passes, and line 14 reads `/etc/passwd`. The same happens when `relative` is a symlink inside home that points outside it. Could you compare `(Path(home) / relative).resolve()` against `Path(home).resolve()` before reading, and add a test that passes `"../outside.txt"`? — Any caller that passes a user-supplied `relative` can read the first 200 characters of any file the process can access, which defeats the "outside home" guard.

(none)

## Suggestions
- app/paths.py:14 — correctness — `candidate.read_text()[:200]` reads and decodes the whole file before keeping 200 characters. For a multi-gigabyte log under home, that loads the entire file into memory. For a binary file such as an image, it reads everything and then raises `UnicodeDecodeError`. Could you open the file and call `f.read(200)` instead? — A preview of a large file uses memory and time in proportion to the file's size instead of a fixed 200 characters.

## Strengths
- `test_preview` checks the 200-character cut-off with a 500-character file and the short-file case with `"hello"`. Both match how `preview` slices.
